question: What is the primary goal of microbial isolation in the laboratory?

options.A: Separating a single microbe from a mixed population
options.B: Destroying all pathogens present on a surface
options.C: Counting the exact total weight of a sample
options.D: Changing the genetic material of bacteria

explanation: Isolation allows technicians to separate individual species from complex mixtures for independent study. [learn more](GST114_U5_T2#GST114_U5_T2_h1)

question: Why are environmental samples usually described as mixed populations?

options.A: They are completely free of any living organisms
options.B: They only contain viruses and fungi
options.C: They consist of thousands of different microbial species
options.D: They always contain only one bacterial strain

explanation: Natural environments harbour diverse communities of bacteria, fungi, and other microbes living side by side. [learn more](GST114_U5_T2#GST114_U5_T2_h1)

question: Which laboratory equipment is standard for achieving complete sterilisation of media?
explanation: Autoclaves use high-pressure steam to reliably destroy all forms of microbial life, including spores. [learn more](GST114_U5_T2#GST114_U5_T2_h2)

question: The main purpose of flaming an inoculating loop before and after use is to achieve what?

options.A: Cool down the glass test tubes quickly
options.B: Change the colour of the bacterial sample
options.C: Prevent contamination of the culture and environment
options.D: Make the metal wire bend more easily

explanation: Red-hot flaming destroys any lingering microbes on the loop so they do not contaminate new media or the workspace. [learn more](GST114_U5_T2#GST114_U5_T2_h2)

question: Water samples collected for microbiological analysis must be placed in which type of container?
explanation: Sterile containers ensure that environmental bacteria from the container itself do not contaminate the water sample. [learn more](GST114_U5_T2#GST114_U5_T2_h3)

question: Why are soil samples typically diluted with sterile saline before being plated out?

options.A: To change the pH of the soil to alkaline
options.B: To reduce the extremely high number of bacteria present
options.C: To kill any dangerous fungi growing in the dirt
options.D: To dissolve all the rocks and minerals in the soil

explanation: Soil contains billions of microbes, so dilution is necessary to yield countable, separated colonies on agar plates. [learn more](GST114_U5_T2#GST114_U5_T2_h3)

question: What is the primary substance used to solidify liquid microbiological media?
explanation: Agar is an algal extract that remains solid at typical incubation temperatures and does not get digested by most bacteria. [learn more](GST114_U5_T2#GST114_U5_T2_h4)

question: Differential culture media are specifically designed to do what?

options.A: Keep anaerobic bacteria alive without oxygen
options.B: Provide zero nutrients so weak microbes can rest
options.C: Stop all bacterial growth except for Staphylococcus species
options.D: Distinguish between different groups of bacteria using colour changes

explanation: Differential media use chemical indicators to highlight metabolic differences between various microbial species on the same plate. [learn more](GST114_U5_T2#GST114_U5_T2_h4)

question: Which inoculation technique is most commonly used to obtain isolated colonies from a mixed culture?
explanation: The streak plate dilutes bacteria mechanically across an agar surface to produce separated, individual colonies. [learn more](GST114_U5_T2#GST114_U5_T2_h5)

question: What happens to the concentration of bacteria as you progress through the quadrants of a proper streak plate?

options.A: It stays exactly the same throughout the plate
options.B: It decreases with each successive quadrant
options.C: It increases rapidly with each stroke
options.D: It disappears completely after the first line

explanation: Diluting the sample across multiple zones thins out the bacteria so individual cells grow into separate colonies. [learn more](GST114_U5_T2#GST114_U5_T2_h5)

question: Gram staining is primarily used to examine which feature of an isolated microorganism?

options.A: Ability to survive in boiling water
options.B: Total weight of the bacterial colony

explanation: Gram staining differentiates bacteria into Gram-positive and Gram-negative based on peptidoglycan layer thickness. [learn more](GST114_U5_T2#GST114_U5_T2_h6)

question: When first inspecting an agar plate, what does colony morphology refer to?

options.A: The type of safety cabinet used during the incubation period
options.B: The internal genetic code inside the bacterial nucleus
options.C: The chemical formula used to make the liquid broth
options.D: The physical appearance of individual bacterial colonies on the agar

explanation: Colony morphology describes visible traits like shape, colour, texture, and edge appearance on a solid medium. [learn more](GST114_U5_T2#GST114_U5_T2_h6)

question: Why are environmental surveillance cultures sometimes performed in hospital wards?

options.A: To test how well the lighting system works in the hallways
options.B: To measure the exact humidity levels in the patient rooms
options.C: To detect hidden pathogens and prevent healthcare-associated infections
options.D: To train nursing students in cooking and food preparation

explanation: Surveillance cultures identify environmental reservoirs of dangerous microbes so cleaning practices can be improved. [learn more](GST114_U5_T2#GST114_U5_T2_h7)

question: A nurse collects a wound swab from a surgical site showing signs of infection. What is the primary purpose of isolating the microbe from this swab?

options.A: To increase the total number of white blood cells in the patient
options.B: To prove that the hospital cleaning staff are performing poorly
options.C: To identify the specific pathogen and guide targeted antibiotic therapy
options.D: To preserve the bacteria in a freezer for future research studies

explanation: Isolating the causative agent allows clinicians to select the most effective antibiotic rather than guessing. [learn more](GST114_U5_T2#GST114_U5_T2_h7)
